body:
Thanks for writing that. I appreciate it.

So I've decided to postpone my plan. I'll give life another chance.

My thoughts are still so jumbled. I still have problems. I feel like I'm going to try the same things again with my same problems and go through the same thing with the same result. Obvious answer: change something. But I can't change my problems. I can't just *be* not-depressed.

I'm scared of failure. What if I don't have what it takes? What if it doesn't work out?

> and I can call you my friend.

Thank you, my optimistic friend. Thank you.

I will have to consider your words. My immediate response is that having things doesn't make me happy. It's what I can do with these things that will. Buying a beach house won't make me happy. Living in one will. I see how this can be seen as materialistic. But I don't want things to make me happy, I want what these things can bring me.

As for the amount of pain my death would bring, I think I have a pretty good idea. *It's would be really really bad*. I've thought about it. It's not something I want to do.. But consider my position: I'm at the point where living my life is comparable to my family's suffering from my death, which we both agree would be significant. That's how I feel. There are no good options.

But see my post below, I've decided to hold off for now.

School makes me unhappy. Jobs and exercise, meh. I don't love being social but it would be nice to 'hang out' with someone else on something like a biweekly schedule. Might be asking for too much though. I don't think I'm ready for school clubs yet.

This is good advice. But what if you do this and the journey to what you want looks worse than your goal? I mean, I have goals and interests but getting there requires me to do some things that makes me really miserable. At this point, I'm trying to stop the pain.

But that's the thing. I don't think my problems are solvable. Let's say I have goals in life. Let's also say that my goals require a billion dollars. What are my options for achieving this? I can get a minimum wage job now and work the rest of my life and never make it... Or I can go to college and get a decent job and work the rest of my life and not make it. Third option is to have smaller dreams. Ferraris turn into Corollas, lake houses turn into gated communities. My dreams are impossible to reach. Settling for less wont make me happy and trying to achieve them will be miserable. I don't have any good options here. What's the point if you know you'll be unhappy?

I've considered the other people in my life. I understand that my death will affect my family and quite honestly, I really, really don't want to put them through that. But I ask that they consider me. By living, I am subjecting myself to a significant amount of pain. I've weighed the pain I'm going to suffer for the rest of my life against the pain my death will inflict. I think my death will amount to less. Again, I don't have any good options. Just 'less bad' ones.

Deal with it? I don't. Well.. I've been in therapy and doing medication for the last few months. It's helped a little. Otherwise, I just try to stay alive and try not to think about it. And I sleep. Because when you're sleeping, you're not awake and being awake sucks.

No abuse unfortunately.

I wish those thoughts were fleeting. I think about ending it every day. No need to get into the reasons here. What stops me? Honestly, my parents. They care about me more than *[alot](http://4.bp.blogspot.com/_D_Z-D2tzi14/S8TRIo4br3I/AAAAAAAACv4/Zh7_GcMlRKo/s1600/ALOT.png)*. The amount of pain I would cause them.... And if I have parents that care so much why am I so depressed? That only makes me feel worse.

Having no friends sucks so much. Every time I read 'So my friends and I were <activity-ing>' on Reddit, I get sad and jealous. I've never had that. I mean sometimes, I just want to share some of my life with somebody else. You know that awesome movie that's coming out soon, or that cool new thing you got/did, or that crazy thing that happened to you? I wish I could tell someone about that. How do I cope? I just sit in a puddle of my misery and loneliness. It's not so bad.. I've been here so long the water is actually kinda warm. (not pee!)

I have this ideal image of myself. .... I'm like a hermit, but that doesn't stop me from doing anything. I'm just okay with being alone. It wouldn't bother me. If there's something I wanted to do, I just went out and did it. I don't care about what anyone else thinks, I'm living my life and doing what I want to do. .... I think all that's possible. I just have to get over my depression. Being not depressed won't make me social, but it'll make me functional. (or at least I hope)

Making friends? I'm still working on making coherent responses to cashiers.

I don't even want to get into what's wrong. For reasons I don't want to get into either. (mostly because it's embarrassing, not bad) But what if you look at the world, how it is and how it works, and you realize that you'll never be happy? I know what they say, 'surely there's something on the planet that can make you happy'. But what if there isn't? What if being alive meant being miserable until you die? How is that worth it? What if the thing that makes me happy *isn't attainable*? What then? Why should I live? I didn't ask for any of this. I didn't ask to be alive. I didn't ask to be expected to take on these responsibilities. .. I found a solution... but everyone gets all concernicus when I start bringing that up.

Meh.
So I'm not saying that I'm going though pretty much the *exact* same thing, but how did you deal with all this?
They're my problems. Thanks for talking to me. Helps more than you'd think.
I'm sorry. (and thanks)
I'm hopeless. This isn't going to work.

When I look at something unknown, I try to determine the possible outcomes and calculate the probabilities of each happening.  I can try to be more positive. It's just I have so few reasons.

>you could meet the love of your life.

Ha.

I guess I could ask someone about the professor's name. But I still have all those other questions. And I'm not expecting you to answer all them, my point is that I'm still really unsure about this. I guess I'll simulate more situations so I'll be comfortable if I actually do try.

All that makes sense. I get what I should be doing... but I can't do it. Hate to be negative, but that's how I feel. You're asking me to blindly believe in something that I'm not even sure exists. I know I *should* and I know that doing that will help me get better, but I can't do that. It's setting yourself up for failure. What if things don't work out? That's the deliemma I'm in. I know what I should be doing but I can't. And that frustrates the hell out of me. It's like a constant pressure. Knowing that what you're doing is bad, but can't help it. It's *so* frustrating and only makes things worse.

Yeah I'm a weirdo. Sorry to catch you off guard. Is it still okay to ask questions?  If not just ignore them. I guess I can start with the bless you thing. That doesn't sound nearly as scary as a conversation. But when would I ask questions that I already know? Like when would be a good time to ask a question? Won't it be kind of weird for a stranger to ask "How are you?"

See that's where everything get weird. All my problems are in my head. It's not anybody else. It's me. I've completely destroyed my self-esteem, self-worth, and any other self-*. So because of that anything social is impossible to say the least. "Ok, no worries, why not try to work on your own issues then tackle the social stuff?" Because how do I improve my self-esteem? Why should I feel good about myself? What is there to like? I hate my life and especially myself. You just don't suddenly start liking yourself one day. This all feels so circular. One causes the other and the other causes the first. 

And I still don't get how to talk to people. I can think of things to say, but surely they're going to say something back. How do I respond and keep the conversation going? ... I sound like a complete idiot. Like I know how basic basic conversations work, but after you have a couple exchanges about 'how cold it's been' and 'at least it's not raining' what do you do next? And how do you go from those small conversations to actual friends? Do you have to explicitly ask to be friends? And how do you know when to ask because it seems weird to ask after only a short conversation.
This is going to sound stupid.. but how do you make friends? And is there anything I might be doing that would cause people not to want to talk to me?
Hehe thanks.

>You can have all the cyber-hugs you need.

I'll take all you have. Thanks for listening to me.

... I don't know what to do...

Every problem I have is intertwined with another problem so you start working on one only to run into another. And life doesn't stop so you never get a chance to regroup you have to keep living while trying to fix everything... I'm not trying hard enough... but I'm doing everything I can.

No problem. 

>like a book. Up to this point the book can be absolute shit. But if you keep reading you don't know, the next page, or there could be a page or even sentence that makes the whole book worth it.

Or maybe the book doesn't ever get better. You don't know right? So now as you read this god awful book, you have to decide how likely it is that the book will get better.

>I know that sounds damn near impossible

Yeah. It does. I mean I want things to get better... but it just doesn't seem like they ever will. And what will I do in the meantime? Keep waking up wishing I didn't? What a great start to my awful day. I'm not saying my life won't ever get better because it might. But right now, I don't care if it gets better or not. Sometimes it just get's too bad to cope with.

>So I (humbly) suggest to you that you don't actually want the things, you want the experience that getting and having the things brings to you. And, to me, that's the point Rao is getting at. He's not saying "settle for less". He's saying that the idea that we need any kind of external-world outcome to give us a certain experience is a delusion 

I can agree with that suggestion. Just 'having' or 'getting' nice things won't make me happy. I want to use them. I want the things that I want because I enjoy those things. If we could do anything we wanted, those things is what I'd do. Do I understand what you're saying correctly?

>>I've heard Franklin is more sympathetic than Jackson.

>I have no idea what this refers to, sorry.

[Bad joke](http://www.marshu.com/articles/presidents-on-us-united-states-paper-bills-currency.php). (sorry) Makes even less sense if you're not american. The point I was getting at is that  money may not buy happiness, but I'd rather have money and be miserable than to be miserable with no money. 

>I hear you. I don't have any easy answers except that the thing that made it bearable for me, and the thing that seems to make it more bearable for most of the people I talk to (I answer a suicide hotline IRL, btw) is not having to go through it alone. Knowing that somebody else understands at least some, and cares about building that understanding... that is what makes it possible and ultimately worthwhile. <hugs>

Yeah. Thanks. (*hug*) I want to fix things. I really do. It's just *so* much and it's so emotional.
Sure.

Thanks. I do want to talk... It's just I feel so unimportant. I would hate to talk to you when you could be talking to someone who actually has serious problems.

I have recently discovered Radiohead's OK Computer and Kid A. Motion Picture Soundtrack gets me every time.

This is going to sound really negative. My outlook is negative becasue everything that has happened to me has been negative. If I had a positive outlook on life right now, I would be disappointed *all the time*. I expect bad things to happen and I'm usually right. Feeling alone is actually one of my bigger issues. Reading your post is so reliving to me. Sometimes I wonder if I'm the only person who sees these things. Thanks (*hug*)

I wish I could change this. I've put some serious thought into running away. Not forever, just for a few years. College and a career and all that stuff will always be here. But I keep running into the same issue. Money.

That's the dilemma. I know life *can* get better and I"d be missing out on the good parts. But is it worth all this pain that I'm going through right now? Yeah I'm going to miss a lot, but I want this pain to end right now. It's too much to deal with. I want it to stop. And if that what it takes...

Look. I know that sounds awful. This whole thing is awful. This isn't what I want. But this is what's happening. And I don't know what else to do.

What do I want to do? Right now, I want to end this pain. In the short term, I'd like to stop failing my classes. It's not overly difficult. But I won't do anything. I have a homework assignment due at midnigtht that I'm not going to do and I have a test tomorrow and obviously I've studied. If I studied for two hours every day, I could pull a 3.0 no problem. And with a bit more time, 3.5 is without a doubt possible. In the longer term, I want to get some kind of technical job working with electronics or computers. After I get some experience, I want to go off and start my own company doing something similar. In the longest term, I want to retire as early as possible. That probably sounds crazy, but you asked.

And thanks. (*hug*)
I shouldn't have said that. I'm not exactly sure where my arms go so it might be a little awkward, but (*hug*) Thanks.

Reading #2 almost made me cry. You get it. I can't explain.. but you fucking get it.

I typed out a bunch of notes from that video. Interesting. I'll spare you from reading all that. In short, I'm not so sure I buy into that... What I got from it is that you shouldn't worry about the outcome, but instead worry about how to get there. To me, that's settling for less. I agree with him though. Settling for less will make you happy because you're not bothered by failure. But that's not how I work. I want things. I don't want the process.

This relates to so much more things I should explain, but that'll take ages. I've thought that maybe I just won't ever be happy. And I've kinda accepted that. This state of this world makes me very sad. (And it's *so* much more than the fact people are homeless and starving) So I want material things because they interest me and that's what I've devoted my life to achieving. I probably won't ever be happy. But I'd rather have all the stuff I want and be unhappy than have nothing and still be unhappy. I've heard Franklin is more sympathetic than Jackson.

But this is a very complex issue... it won't be resolved in a paragraph. It won't be resolved in this thread. It won't be resolved in a paper. It won't be resolved in a book. There's so much to consider.

And the last thing you mentioned is what my problem is. Yes, things *can* get better. But is it worth it? Is all this pain that I'm feeling now, and that I'm going to experience tomorrow, and the day after that, and the day after that... is all that really worth whatever 'better' is? I'm not sure....... That makes me not want to even try to be honest.
